quickSummary: The Electron Transport System (ETS) comprises four inner mitochondrial membrane-bound protein complexes (I–IV) and two mobile carriers (Ubiquinone/CoQ and Cytochrome c). Complex I (NADH-CoQ oxidoreductase) pumps 4 H⁺; Complex II (Succinate-CoQ oxidoreductase) transfers electrons from FADH₂ without pumping protons; Complex III (CoQH₂-Cyt c oxidoreductase) pumps 4 H⁺ via the Q-cycle; and Complex IV (Cytochrome c oxidase) transfers electrons to terminal O₂ to form H₂O while pumping 2 H⁺. Specific inhibitors include Rotenone (I), Malonate (II), Antimycin A (III), and Cyanide/Azide/CO (IV).

conceptBreakdown.content:
The respiratory Electron Transport System (ETS) is located in the **inner mitochondrial membrane** (cristae). It transfers electrons from $\text{NADH}$ and $\text{FADH}_2$ down a redox potential gradient to molecular oxygen ($\text{O}_2$), the terminal electron acceptor, coupling electron flux to proton translocation from the matrix into the **intermembrane space**.

- **Complex I ($\text{NADH}$-CoQ Oxidoreductase)**: Binds matrix $\text{NADH}$, transferring $2\text{e}^-$ through $\text{FMN}$ and $8\text{--}9\text{ Fe-S}$ clusters to Ubiquinone (CoQ), pumping **$4\text{ H}^+$** across the membrane.
- **Complex II (Succinate-CoQ Oxidoreductase)**: Contains Succinate Dehydrogenase; transfers $2\text{e}^-$ from succinate via bound $\text{FAD}$ and $\text{Fe-S}$ to CoQ. It does **not span the bilayer** and translocates **$0\text{ H}^+$**.
- **Complex III (CoQH$_2$-Cytochrome $c$ Oxidoreductase)**: Oxidizes $\text{CoQH}_2$ and reduces Cytochrome $c$ via the bifurcated **Q-Cycle**, pumping **$4\text{ H}^+$**.
- **Complex IV (Cytochrome $c$ Oxidase)**: Contains Cytochrome $a$, Cytochrome $a_3$, and copper centers ($\text{Cu}_A$ and $\text{Cu}_B$). Reduces $\text{O}_2$ to water ($4\text{e}^- + 4\text{H}^+ + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$) and pumps **$2\text{ H}^+$** per electron pair.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### Respiratory Complexes & Specific Inhibitors Matrix

| Complex | Official Name | Prosthetic Groups / Components | $H^+$ Translocated per $2\text{e}^-$ | Specific Inhibitors |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Complex I** | **$\text{NADH}$-CoQ Oxidoreductase** | $\text{FMN}$, $8\text{--}9$ Iron-Sulfur ($\text{Fe-S}$) centers | **$4\text{ H}^+$** | **Rotenone**, Amytal, Piericidin A |
| **Complex II** | **Succinate-CoQ Oxidoreductase** | $\text{FAD}$, $3\text{ Fe-S}$ centers, Cytochrome $b_{560}$ | **$0\text{ H}^+$** (Does not span membrane) | **Malonate**, Oxaloacetate, TTFA |
| **Complex III** | **CoQH$_2$-Cytochrome $c$ Oxidoreductase** | Cytochrome $b_L$, Cytochrome $b_H$, Rieske $\text{Fe-S}$, Cytochrome $c_1$ | **$4\text{ H}^+$** (via Q-Cycle) | **Antimycin A**, Myxothiazol |
| **Complex IV** | **Cytochrome $c$ Oxidase** | Cytochrome $a$, Cytochrome $a_3$, $\text{Cu}_A$ and $\text{Cu}_B$ copper centers | **$2\text{ H}^+$** | **Cyanide ($\text{CN}^-$)**, Carbon Monoxide ($\text{CO}$), Sodium Azide ($\text{NaN}_3$) |

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Mobile Electron Carriers (CoQ & Cytochrome c)
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Mobile Electron Carriers (CoQ & Cytochrome c)
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Ubiquinone (Coenzyme Q / CoQ)**:
   - A small, hydrophobic, lipid-soluble benzoquinone dissolved within the lipid core of the inner membrane.
   - Acts as a mobile electron and proton carrier, collecting reducing equivalents from both Complex I and Complex II and delivering them to Complex III.
2. **Cytochrome c**:
   - A small, water-soluble peripheral hemeprotein electrostatically attached to the outer surface of the inner mitochondrial membrane (facing the intermembrane space).
   - Shuttles electrons single-file from Complex III (Cytochrome $c_1$) to Complex IV (Cytochrome $a$).
